artbip

Live with great paintings.

artbip is a free Mac app that sets a different public-domain painting as your desktop wallpaper, using museum-quality scans from the Met, the Rijksmuseum, the Art Institute of Chicago, and other open-access collections.

Download for macOS View source on GitHub Free & open source · macOS 15+ · no account, no telemetry
Why this exists

An old app taught me to recognize paintings.

Ten years ago I ran a small app called Artpip that changed my wallpaper to a different painting every hour. I never studied art, and I didn't study it then either. But last spring, standing in a gallery in front of a canvas I had never seen in person, I realized I already knew it. That painting had spent a week behind my terminal windows a decade earlier.

Artpip is gone now. The company folded, the servers went dark, and the app stopped working. That seemed like the wrong ending for something whose whole job was showing five-hundred-year-old paintings, so I rebuilt it in a way that doesn't depend on anyone staying in business. The collection is a plain file in an open-source repository, the images come from the museums' own open-access programs, and there is no server behind any of it.

It runs in the menu bar, changes the picture on a schedule you pick, and otherwise stays out of the way.

The collection

Two thousand paintings, chosen carefully.

A curated collection

The 2,000 works were chosen from 4,653 candidates gathered across six museum open-access programs. Each candidate was scored on significance and on how well it holds up as something you look at all day, with a cap on any single artist so the mix stays broad.

Nothing gets cropped

Most wallpaper apps crop paintings to fit the screen. artbip composes the whole painting over a blurred version of itself, or over a flat colour taken from its palette, so portraits and panoramas keep their real proportions.

Wall labels

An optional caption in the corner shows the title, artist, date, and a sentence or two about the work, written in the style of a museum label.

Ask about a painting

A panel tells you who painted the picture, what tradition it belongs to, and what any symbols in it traditionally mean. Every claim lists the book and page it came from.

Museum scans

Images come from the museums' own open-access endpoints at up to 4K, and are composed separately for each of your displays at its exact resolution.

Favourites and history

A searchable gallery shows the whole collection. You can favourite works, rotate only favourites, block anything permanently, and look up what was on screen last Tuesday.

No server

artbip is a native Swift app with no account, no telemetry, and no backend. Once images are cached it works offline. The collection itself is a readable JSON file that records the public-domain evidence for every work.

Questions

Things people ask.

Is this legal?

Yes. Every work is public domain or CC0, and artbip records the evidence for each one (the museum's own public-domain flag, or Wikimedia's licence data) along with a link to the source.

Does it phone home?

No. There is no server, no account, and no analytics. The app talks only to the museum and Wikimedia image hosts named in the collection file, caches what it fetches, and works offline after that.

Will it die like Artpip did?

There is nothing to shut down. The collection is a file in the repository, the images are hosted by the museums, and the code is open source. It keeps working whether or not I do.

What does it cost in battery?

Very little. It wakes on your chosen interval, composes one image, sets it as the wallpaper, and goes back to sleep.
